name: Welch-Dickey Loop
where: Orris Road trailhead, Thornton, near Waterville Valley, New Hampshire
blurb: Two bare granite summits at the gateway to Waterville Valley: a short climb to the Welch Ledges, Dickey Mountain up its slabs, and the classic loop over both.

trails.name: Dickey Mountain via the Dickey side

status: Open. No closures listed by the White Mountain National Forest as of November 2026. $5 per vehicle day-use fee at the Orris Road lot; the bare ledges are icy from fall to spring, so carry traction.
notes: No animal on these trails is flagged as rare. The notable rarity is a plant: Welch is one of five New Hampshire sites where jack pine survives (USFS trail sheet); it is drawn as a landmark and named in the Welch summit stop. B's 4.0 mi is derived from the USFS segment distance (Dickey summit to parking 2.0 mi). Animals documented (iNaturalist within 2 km, Spicebush 2012 trip report) but not modeled for lack of a model: snowshoe hare, eastern milksnake, eastern newt, salamanders, toads/frogs, dark-eyed junco, warblers, kinglets, mourning dove.
